findings.issue: The hook says "six hours cost more than seven" but row 2 is 7.50 hours, not seven. A viewer reading the sheet sees 7.50 and the line is a beat off.
findings.fix: Either reword the body to "six hours cost more\nthan seven and a half" or change A2 to 7.00 (B2 becomes 294.00) so the hook is literally what's on screen.

findings.issue: "F4 cycles the dollar signs" is true on Windows Excel; on Mac it's Command+T (F4 only works if function keys are remapped). Small unqualified claim.
findings.fix: Either drop the F4 clause (the reel doesn't need it) or say "F4 on Windows cycles the dollar signs."

findings.issue: Two captions in a row with the same grammatical shape (bare noun-phrase fragments, comma list). Reads like a template.
findings.fix: Rewrite one as a full sentence a person would text, e.g. "The rates live in a table\nfurther down."

findings.issue: A rate table used to multiply hours that includes Mileage at 0.67 (a per-mile rate) is a slight logical wobble, and the A7 label "Rate table" reads like a title dropped into a data cell.
findings.fix: Label A7 "Rate type" and consider swapping Mileage for a third labor rate (Shop, Subcontract) or leave Mileage but keep the header honest.

findings.issue: "Anything that shouldn't move needs dollar signs" and "If it shouldn't move, put dollar signs on it" are the same sentence twice back to back.
findings.fix: Make the sub concrete instead of a restatement, e.g. "The rate cell never moves. B8 stays B8."

findings.issue: Hours / labor cost is job costing rather than an accounting-system export, and the reel isn't tagged as the weekly [general] tip. Fine, but it's the generic side of the ground you claim.
findings.fix: If this fills the general slot, mark it as such; otherwise ground it as a job-cost sheet built from a time export (add a job or cost code column label in A1's row wording only, no schema change).

hook.note: "378.00 / six hours cost more than seven" is a real symptom, concrete, on-sheet, and under 10 words. It asks the viewer to do one step of arithmetic to feel the wrong, which costs a little punch; the 7.50 vs "seven" mismatch costs a little more. Fix that and it's a 5.

claims.claim: Dragging =A2*B8 down one row makes it =A3*B9 (relative reference shifts one row per row)
claims.note: Standard relative reference behaviour in every Excel version.

claims.claim: 6.00 hours at the overtime rate of 63.00 gives 378.00, more than 7.50 hours at 42.00 (315.00)
claims.note: Arithmetic holds; also confirmed by the verification block.

claims.claim: $B$8 locks both row and column so the reference doesn't move when filled down
claims.note: Correct; column lock is redundant for a vertical fill but the reel says "row and column, both" as a habit, not as a necessity, which is fair.

claims.claim: "Drag it now and every row still reads B8"

claims.note: True on Windows Excel; Mac uses Command+T. Add "on Windows" or cut.

claims.claim: Absolute references work in Excel 2016/2019 as shown
claims.note: No modern-only function used, so no version caveat needed.

claims.claim: Premise that the formula was right in row 2 and only broke on the drag
claims.note: B2 = 315.00 is consistent with =A2*B8; no mutation block, so nothing to check against an insert.
